messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
char c = 'a';
if (c == "a") fire(); else open_door();

Question: What happens?
The student answered: it fires

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: `==` compares text

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: long-winded, walks through the steps one by one, 20 to 35 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["First c gets the value a, then the if checks c equals the text a, both look same so condition true, fire runs.", "Looking at the if line, c holds a and the quotes around a mean the same thing, so comparing them matches and fire happens.", "c is set to a, then compared with a in quotes, characters and text match here, so open_door is skipped and fire runs.", "Right side of == is the text a, left side c is also a, equality holds true, so it goes into fire branch.", "The if condition checks c against a, sees they are equal, so the true block runs and fire gets called first."]}

sentences: First c gets the value a, then the if checks c equals the text a, both look same so condition true, fire runs.
Looking at the if line, c holds a and the quotes around a mean the same thing, so comparing them matches and fire happens.
c is set to a, then compared with a in quotes, characters and text match here, so open_door is skipped and fire runs.
Right side of == is the text a, left side c is also a, equality holds true, so it goes into fire branch.
The if condition checks c against a, sees they are equal, so the true block runs and fire gets called first.
